aspects.says: An override may declare fewer or narrower checked exceptions, never broader ones, and a caller must handle what the type it calls through declares.
basis: section:An Override May Narrow the Return Type and the Checked Exceptions, Never Widen Them

aspects.says: An override may narrow a reference return type to a subtype, and javac adds a bridge method for callers of the wider type; a wider return type does not compile.
basis: section:An Override May Narrow the Return Type and the Checked Exceptions, Never Widen Them

aspects.says: Absence of many results is an empty collection, not null and not an Optional of a collection; Optional is meant for return types, not fields or parameters.
basis: section:Put Absence in the Return Type: an Empty Optional or an Empty Collection, Never null
aspects.reason: a design guideline with no wrong output to observe beyond the empty, editable result that the clinic-waitlist practice checks

aspects.says: final on a parameter only stops the method's body from reassigning it; it is not part of the signature, and an override may drop it.
basis: section:An Override May Narrow the Return Type and the Checked Exceptions, Never Widen Them
aspects.reason: a compile-time rule: a reassignment the compiler refuses has no wrong solution that compiles, and nothing at run time differs

aspects.says: Inside a generic method the varargs array of a type variable is built with the erased type, so handing it out as T[] causes a ClassCastException in a caller with no cast.
basis: section:A Generic Varargs Array Has the Erased Type, So Handing It Out Fails Somewhere Else
section:Spot the Problem: a Generic Method That Returns Its Varargs Array

aspects.says: A value that may be missing is returned as an Optional built with ofNullable, since Optional.of throws on null and a bare null fails at the caller.
basis: section:Put Absence in the Return Type: an Empty Optional or an Empty Collection, Never null

aspects.says: Optional.orElse evaluates its argument whether or not a value is present; orElseGet calls its supplier only when the Optional is empty.
basis: section:Put Absence in the Return Type: an Empty Optional or an Empty Collection, Never null

aspects.says: A method that returns its internal collection gives every caller write access to it; returning a copy keeps the caller's changes, and later changes to the owner, apart.
basis: section:A Returned Collection Is Whatever the Caller Can Do With It

aspects.says: @SafeVarargs silences the heap-pollution warnings without checking anything, and is allowed only on constructors and static, final or private methods.
basis: section:Spot the Problem: a Generic Method That Returns Its Varargs Array
aspects.reason: an annotation rule the compiler enforces and a warning it prints; a graded run sees neither, and the runtime failure is the same with or without the annotation

aspects.says: A method returns the same kind of collection on every path, so an empty result is as editable as a full one.
basis: section:A Returned Collection Is Whatever the Caller Can Do With It

aspects.says: A reference array that fits the varargs array type is passed as the array, while a primitive array becomes a single element.
basis: section:A Varargs Parameter Is an Array: the Caller Can Pass Its Own, or null

aspects.says: A null argument to a varargs parameter arrives as a null array, not as an array holding one null, so the method must decide what a null array means.
basis: section:A Varargs Parameter Is an Array: the Caller Can Pass Its Own, or null

aspects.says: An array passed to a varargs parameter becomes the parameter itself, so the method shares the caller's array: sorting it or keeping it reaches the caller.
basis: section:A Varargs Parameter Is an Array: the Caller Can Pass Its Own, or null
